![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200586/assets/8524ffd2ff653703bd6fcfa2b44d36821aeb34877d58bbc6df388497cac8e07d.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $x$-axis and the lines $y=2x$ and $y=4-2x$, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{x}{2}.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le 2-\frac{y}{2}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200586/assets/293f8454cdda5897de111d6444baa4674eccf28a36e2053f3f2cb71f948e07fe.png)

  

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{2-y/2}\frac{x}{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{2-y/2}x(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}-4y+4)[{\int }_{y/2}^{2-y/2}x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}-4y+4){[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=y/2}^{x=2-y/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}-4y+4)\cdot \frac{1}{2}[{(2-\frac{y}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{y}{2})}^{2}]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}-4y+4)(4-2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}-2{y}^{3}+12{y}^{2}-24y+16\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[-\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}+4{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}+16y]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-8+32-48+32) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 1,\,\,1\le y\le 2\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=y-x.$ Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=-2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=-2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-(-2)|=|x+2|.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)|x+2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y(x+2)^{2}-x(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}(x+2)^{2}-xy(x+2)^{2}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(3-2x)(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{1}(-2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+4x+12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{-{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3}+2{x}^{2}+12x]}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{5}{3}+2+12)-(-8+\frac{40}{3}+8-24)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((14-\frac{13}{6})-(-24+\frac{40}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{135}{6}) \\  & =\frac{45}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 5,\,\,1\le y\le 2\}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=3\cdot 1=3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{M}{3}|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{M}{3}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}({\int }_{2}^{5}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(x-2)^{3}]_{2}^{5}\cdot {[y]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(\frac{1}{3}(5-2)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(2-2)^{3})\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(9-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $x=\sqrt{2y}$ and $x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{4}{3},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2y}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200586/assets/d9c529fe2d238a3d6ac4e20cfcd571f980c28a4eb2c13497fab3ccb0d15ac6eb.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{3M}{4}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}\frac{3M}{4}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}[x]_{x={y}^{2}/2}^{x=\sqrt{2y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}(\sqrt{2y}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\sqrt{2}{y}^{5/2}-\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}-4\sqrt{2}{y}^{3/2}+2{y}^{3}+4\sqrt{2}{y}^{1/2}-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{[\frac{2\sqrt{2}{y}^{7/2}}{7}-\frac{{y}^{5}}{10}-\frac{8\sqrt{2}{y}^{5/2}}{5}+\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}+\frac{8\sqrt{2}{y}^{3/2}}{3}-\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}(\frac{32}{7}-\frac{32}{10}-\frac{64}{5}+8+\frac{32}{3}-\frac{16}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}(\frac{40}{21}) \\  & =\frac{10M}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200586/assets/de1ac9ccf84134913bbf8847ea9795a1ec83084602db705c8bef723897e7bd92.png)

A triangular plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ in the first quadrant enclosed between the axes and the line $y=1-x.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1-x\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200586/assets/a092d57585bd7b2803473c30328dd72f82a6611d8398de821099db72e2ed3621.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=3$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-3|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|x|=kx,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}kx\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}x{[y]}_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}x(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}x-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=kx=6Mx.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}6Mx\,|x-3{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}6Mx(x-3)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =6M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+9x)[{\int }_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =6M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+9x){[y]}_{0}^{1-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+9x)(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6M{\int }_{0}^{1}(-{x}^{4}+7{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}+9x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6M{[-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{7}{4}{x}^{4}-5{x}^{3}+\frac{9}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =6M[-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{7}{4}-5+\frac{9}{2}-0] \\  & =6M[\frac{21}{20}] \\  & =\frac{63M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
